newsitem.title: USA: Amoco has glitch at Texas refinery at weekend.
newsitem.headline: Amoco has glitch at Texas refinery at weekend.

text.p: Amoco Corp had a brief glitch over the weekend at its Texas City, Texas refinery, the largest in the United States, according to state environmental officials.
"They had a faulty analyzer at a vapor recovery unit which caused a compressor to go out," said Patrick Shaughnessy at the Texas Natural Resources Conservation Commission.

Shaughnessy said Amoco had the problem early Saturday before sunrise, but could not elaborate on how the problem affected overall operations at the plant. Officials at Amoco meanwhile declined to comment on operations at the plant.

But the revelation of a small problem at Texas City, where Amoco has crude distillation capacity of 433,000 barrels per day (bpd), follows talk among some traders that Amoco is now involved in some sort of winter maintenance at the huge plant.
It was not clear from that talk what kind of maintenance, if any, Amoco was undertaking.
Amoco also has 204,000 bpd catalytic cracking capacity at the facility.
A vapor recovery unit turns hydrocarbon vapors back into liquid form for further processing, transport or storage.
